title: Evaluation along a section under composite exceptional adjunction
statement:
Use the global finite-field and finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ with $n\ge1$. Work with the geometric derived operations on $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, using the specified constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]. All tensor products and pullbacks below are derived, with the signed symmetry of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $f:Z\to X$ and $j:X\to Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with $f\circ j=\operatorname{id}_X$. Let $D,K,W\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and let $v:D\otimes K\to W$ be any morphism. Let $l:Rj_!K\to Rf^!K$ be the $Rj_!\dashv Rj^!$ adjunct of the inverse composition identification $K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!Rf^!K$ for $fj=\operatorname{id}_X$. Define $V:Lf^*D\otimes Rf^!K\to Rf^!W$ to be the $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ adjunct of
$$
Rf_!(Lf^*D\otimes Rf^!K)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}^{-1}}D\otimes Rf_!Rf^!K\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_f}D\otimes K\xrightarrow{v}W.
$$
The projection formula here and below is that of [prop-functor-package](5), with the signed symmetries to put the pullback factor first. Let
$$
\theta:Rj_!(D\otimes K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*D\otimes Rj_!K
$$
be its inverse for $j$, using $Lj^*Lf^*D\cong D$. Then the $j$-adjoint of $V\circ(1\otimes l)\circ\theta$, followed by the exceptional composition identification for $fj=\operatorname{id}_X$, is exactly $v$:
$$
\bigl(Rj^!Rf^!W\xrightarrow{\sim}W\bigr)\circ\operatorname{adj}_j\bigl(V\circ(1\otimes l)\circ\theta\bigr)=v.
$$
The composition identifications and composite Hom bijections are the ones specified in [def-trf-admissibility] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].

proof.text: Use pullback-first notation $P_h(B,M):B\otimes Rh_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_!(Lh^*B\otimes M)$ for the projection isomorphism, with the signed symmetry inserted on both sides of the formula in [fix-prop-projection-formula]. This theorem supplies naturality and compatibility with compact-support composition for these actual geometric maps. Its hypotheses hold: $h=f,j$ are separated finite type, and every displayed tensor factor is on the finite-Tor constructible domain stipulated in the item. In particular $\theta=P_j(Lf^*D,K)^{-1}$, with $Lj^*Lf^*D=D$. Also $P_{\mathrm{id}}(B,M)=1$: in [def-exchange-projection] take the compactification with both factors identities. The pullback tensor comparison, adjunction unit and counit, and open-extension tensor map are identities under the canonical identity identifications, so the defining projection composite is identity; the two symmetry insertions cancel. This uses the specified geometric projection map, rather than an arbitrary natural isomorphism of its type.

source.place: Step 3(d): the projection-formula evaluation against the section counit, for p_1 Delta = id_X

proof.text:
Write $c_N:Rj^!Rf^!N\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ and $a_M:Rf_!Rj_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the specified comparisons for $fj=\mathrm{id}_X$. By [def-trf-admissibility], $c$ is the adjunction conjugate of $a$, using the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Consequently the composite bijection sends $a_K$ to $c_K^{-1}$. The defining equality $\operatorname{adj}_j(l)=c_K^{-1}$ therefore gives $l=\operatorname{adj}_f(a_K)$. Taking the inverse $f$-adjunction yields
$$\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(l)=a_K.$$
This is only evaluation of the specified two inverse Hom bijections; no full faithfulness of $Rj_!$ or $Rf^!$ is used.

source.place: Step 3(d): the projection-formula evaluation against the section counit, for p_1 Delta = id_X

proof.text:
Put $T=V\circ(1\otimes l)\circ\theta$ and $b=\varepsilon_{f,W}\circ Rf_!T:Rf_!Rj_!(D\otimes K)\to W$. The definition of $V$ as an $f$-adjunct gives
$$\varepsilon_{f,W}\circ Rf_!V=v\circ(1_D\otimes\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ P_f(D,Rf^!K)^{-1}.$$
Apply naturality of the inverse projection isomorphism in its second variable to the morphism $l:Rj_!K\to Rf^!K$:
$$P_f(D,Rf^!K)^{-1}\circ Rf_!(1\otimes l)=(1_D\otimes Rf_!l)\circ P_f(D,Rj_!K)^{-1}.$$
Substitution, functoriality of tensor, and Step 2 give the explicit formula
$$b=v\circ(1_D\otimes a_K)\circ P_f(D,Rj_!K)^{-1}\circ Rf_!\theta.$$
Only naturality of the actual projection map from [fix-prop-projection-formula] and the counit formula for the adjunction of [def-trf-admissibility] enter this calculation.

source.place: Step 3(d): the projection-formula evaluation against the section counit, for p_1 Delta = id_X

proof.text:
Apply the composition compatibility of [fix-prop-projection-formula] to $X\xrightarrow jZ\xrightarrow fX$, with base tensor factor $D$ and source object $K$. In the notation of Step 1 its equation is
$$a_{D\otimes K}\circ Rf_!P_j(Lf^*D,K)\circ P_f(D,Rj_!K)=P_{\mathrm{id}}(D,K)\circ(1_D\otimes a_K)=1_D\otimes a_K.$$
The pullback comparison is $Lj^*Lf^*D=D$. Multiply this equality on the right by $P_f(D,Rj_!K)^{-1}\circ Rf_!\theta$; since $\theta=P_j(Lf^*D,K)^{-1}$, functoriality cancels the adjacent inverse pair. Thus
$$ (1_D\otimes a_K)\circ P_f(D,Rj_!K)^{-1}\circ Rf_!\theta=a_{D\otimes K}.$$
Step 3 now reads $b=v\circ a_{D\otimes K}$. All symmetry constraints are precisely those defining $P_f,P_j$; no permutation of $D$ and $K$ is discarded.

source.place: Step 3(d): the projection-formula evaluation against the section counit, for p_1 Delta = id_X

proof.text: Finally, $T=\operatorname{adj}_f(b)$ by the inverse counit formula for the $f$-adjunction. The composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with the comparisons fixed in [def-trf-admissibility], sends $b=v\circ a_{D\otimes K}$ to $v$, because its identification with the identity adjunction is induced by $a$ and $c$. Its value on $b$ is, by its definition as two successive Hom bijections, $c_W\circ\operatorname{adj}_j(T)$. Hence $c_W\circ\operatorname{adj}_j(V\circ(1\otimes l)\circ\theta)=v$, as asserted.
